stem: Section 14 of the act barred Chinese from becoming citizens. What does that show about the act's purpose?

stimulus.source_note: Chinese Exclusion Act, 22 Stat. 58, approved May 6, 1882. Public domain. Text verified against the Avalon Project (Yale Law School) and the Gilder Lehrman Institute transcription.
stimulus.text:
Chinese Exclusion Act, May 6, 1882 (ellipses mark omissions):

"Whereas, in the opinion of the Government of the United States the coming of Chinese laborers to this country endangers the good order of certain localities within the territory thereof: Therefore, Be it enacted ... That from and after the expiration of ninety days next after the passage of this act, and until the expiration of ten years next after the passage of this act, the coming of Chinese laborers to the United States be, and the same is hereby, suspended..."

"SEC. 14. That hereafter no State court or court of the United States shall admit Chinese to citizenship..."

"SEC. 15. That the words 'Chinese laborers,' wherever used in this act, shall be construed to mean both skilled and unskilled laborers and Chinese employed in mining."

options.text: It was a temporary wartime measure
options.misconception: Background: there was no war with China, and the act reaches beyond any ten-year pause into citizenship itself.

options.text: It applied only to laborers already in the United States
options.misconception: Background: the act suspends the coming of new laborers; Section 14 reaches further, to citizenship itself.

options.text: It aimed at permanent exclusion, not just a pause in immigration
It protected Chinese merchants and students above all
options.misconception: Background: merchants and students were exempted from the ban, but the act's weight fell on laborers.

rationales.A: Background: there was no war with China, and the act reaches beyond any ten-year pause into citizenship itself.
rationales.B: Background: the act suspends the coming of new laborers. Section 14 reaches further, to citizenship itself.
rationales.C: A ten-year pause on arrivals is one thing; a ban on ever becoming a citizen is another. Section 14 shows Congress meant to keep Chinese in America permanently outside the political community.
rationales.D: Background: merchants and students were exempted from the ban, but the act's weight fell on laborers.
rationales.general:
Picture a laborer who has lived and worked in California for years, asking to become a citizen.
1. Read what Section 14 says to him. No court shall admit Chinese to citizenship.
2. Ask what a ten-year pause would need. Only a closed border, not a closed courthouse.
3. Name the purpose. Not a pause, but a permanent line around who can belong.
Remember: a law's longest shadow is the right it takes away forever, not the door it closes for a decade.
